title: Al-Hakim, the All-Wise
tomorrow: why does 'the Loving' sit right beside 'the Forgiving'?

cards: A group project where the smartest person makes a move nobody understands, and says: trust me, I'll explain later. Now put that on a river.

In Surah Al-Kahf, the prophet Musa asks to travel with a servant of God, a man given knowledge from God's own presence; the hadith call him Khidr. Khidr agrees on one condition: ask me nothing until I explain.
They're taken aboard a boat by its owners, poor men who work the water, and Khidr calmly knocks a hole in its side.

teach.b: Musa can't hold it in: you've holed their boat! Khidr reminds him of the deal. Two more scenes follow, each harder to watch, until Musa breaks the deal a third time, and Khidr explains everything.

teach.h: THE KING, THE WALL, THE TREASURE.
teach.b: A king up the river was seizing every sound boat by force. A damaged one would be left for its poor owners. The broken wall Khidr rebuilt for free, in a town that refused them food?
A treasure for two orphan boys lay beneath it, kept safe until they grew up. What looked like damage was protection.

teach.h: AL-HAKIM: EACH THING IN ITS PLACE.
teach.b: That's today's Name: Al-Hakim, the All-Wise, whose wisdom puts each thing in its place, even when the place makes no sense from where you stand.
When the angels in Surah Al-Baqarah admit what they don't know, they say: "Be glorified! We have no knowledge saving that which Thou hast taught us. Lo! Thou, only Thou, art the Knower, the Wise."
And notice what the Qur'an keeps in. Musa objects every time, out loud, and the story doesn't cut it. Trusting a wisdom you can't see isn't pretending nothing's wrong.

teach.h: STAY ON THE BOAT WHILE YOU ASK.
teach.b: It's staying on the boat while you ask.

Here's the detail to tell a friend tonight. In Sahih al-Bukhari, the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, says he wished Musa had been patient a little longer, so that more of their story would have been told.

how: Hadith encourage reciting Surah Al-Kahf, which tells the story of Musa and Khidr, on Fridays; al-Hakim is called on in du'a among the Names.

o: the one who settles disputes between people
the All-Wise, who puts each thing in its place
the healer who knows the cure for every illness

games.q: what happened on the journey — tap the pairs.
p: holed to save it from a king

s: Khidr holed the boat to punish its owners
a king was seizing every sound boat; a damaged one would be left for its poor owners.
Musa broke his promise not to ask more than once
three times, and the third ended the journey (18:71–78).
the name Khidr appears in the Qur'an's telling
the Qur'an calls him a servant of God; the name comes from the hadith.

games.q: you're Musa. the man you promised not to question just knocked a hole in a poor man's boat. what do you do?
o: keep your promise and say nothing.
object out loud, promise or not.
get off the boat and leave him.
games.why: Musa objects: you've holed their boat! the Qur'an keeps his protest in. only later does Khidr explain the king who was seizing every sound boat.

practice: Look at one thing near you that you didn't understand at first: a scar, a hand-me-down, a book someone pushed on you, a gift that seemed odd. Rest your eyes on it, or on its memory, for a few slow breaths.
Then let the sit hold a quiet question: what else might not be in its place yet, from where I stand?

wordCard.voice: Al-Hakim. The All-Wise, who puts each thing in its place, boats and walls included. Name forty-six.

orig.note: Arabic: the All-Wise. in 2:32 the angels say: Thou art the Knower, the Wise.

carryVoice: Keep this: wise, because a hole in a boat can be a rescue. That's day ninety-four.

sources.q: Be glorified! We have no knowledge saving that which Thou hast taught us. Lo! Thou, only Thou, art the Knower, the Wise.

sources.ref: Qur'an 18:65–82 (Musa and the servant of God: the boat, the boy, the wall, and the explanations)
Sahih al-Bukhari 3401, 4725 (the servant is named al-Khidr; the Prophet ﷺ wishes Musa had been patient so more would be told)
